trickyParts: `dnsutils` is a virtual package in Debian trixie with no candidate of its own (apt-cache policy says Candidate: (none)); apt resolves it to its single provider, bind9-dnsutils. The apt line, the three Dockerfile comments, the shipped notices sentence and the docs all name bind9-dnsutils now, so the notices sentence's /usr/share/doc/<package>/copyright claim is true and the build does not depend on one provider staying unique.

`nc` is not a file of netcat-openbsd: the package ships /usr/bin/nc.openbsd and the alternatives system installs the `nc` name as root during the build. Every gate asks for `nc`; the Job proved /usr/bin/nc resolves in the built image.

`nc -h` and `dig -v` take no --version: nc -h prints its usage and exits 0 (OpenBSD netcat, Debian patchlevel 1.229-1), dig -v prints its version on stderr. Both are in the build's toolchain smoke step in that form.

psql in Debian is a Perl wrapper around the versioned client; it resolves because perl-base is already in the image. The Job ran `psql --version` in the built image and got psql (PostgreSQL) 17.11, so the wrapper works there — this is the one tool the rejected .deb-extraction route could not deliver.
The image's /bin/sh is dash, whose `type` builtin has no -P, so the on-PATH check runs as `bash -c 'type -P …'` inside the Job rather than from the harness's shell.

The capability row was extended rather than added: a row renders as name, status and detail with no tool list, so packages/contracts/src/legion-api.ts, the daemon API golden fixture and the end-to-end scripts that enumerate rows by name are untouched.
deviations: The plan's evidence rule asked for the `Setting up <package>` lines counted per stage in the build's own log. The build run (40126149608) had not finished when this phase completed, and `gh run view --log` serves nothing until it does; waiting on CI is forbidden. The stronger evidence was taken instead and is above: the five tools run in a pod of the image that build published (tag sha-839ab9e81bfe), and the image's own `legion probe-image` names them in its toolchain row.

The plan's last section offers restoring a psql example to INFRA-71's section once the tool exists. sjawhar/legion#2092 is still open with changes requested, so there is nothing here to edit without colliding with it; the forward-merge the plan prescribes will land it, and this is left to the architect's call rather than taken unilaterally.

The deployment pins ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker@sha256:e669e39dae705a9475583b14ac1fdc2e152c214ec5378a8d6b6760829e558379 today. discoveredComplexity: The admission policy of the namespace this role can submit Jobs to requires, in this order of refusal: automountServiceAccountToken: false on the pod template, the build compute class in its nodeSelector, runtimeClassName gvisor, activeDeadlineSeconds on the pod template, and a container requesting at least 4 CPU. Each refusal names what it wants, so a server-side dry run finds the next one; the tester can rebuild the Job from this list in five dry runs or fewer.
